# Enterobacterales

> *How do harmless gut residents and dangerous strains of the same species differ?*

::: {.callout-note}
## In preparation
This chapter will follow the same template as the *Gram-positive cocci* chapter. The outline below
shows what it will cover.
:::

**The group in one sentence:** Gram-negative rods that ferment sugars, cope with or without oxygen, and live in the gut.

**How members differ (the sorting key):** Extra genes (toxins, adhesins, capsules); lactose fermentation as a lab readout.

**Main organisms (full profile cards):** *E. coli* (residents versus strains with extra genes), *Klebsiella* (capsule), *Salmonella* (survival inside cells).

**Supporting organisms (one table row each):** *Shigella*, *Proteus*, *Yersinia*.

**Later in the course:** Gut, urinary and bloodstream infections in the organ blocks; resistant strains in pharmacology.
